causal_question: Have human greenhouse-gas emissions caused the observed industrial-era global warming?

chain.evidence: emissions inventories, fuel and industry statistics, land-use estimates
direct atmospheric measurements and historical ice-air records
spectroscopy, radiative-transfer calculations, observed gas abundance
ocean heat, land warming, ice loss, atmospheric warming
multiple independently produced observational temperature datasets
observed warming is reproduced by simulations with human and natural forcing, not natural forcing alone

dashboard_conclusion: Greenhouse gases caused more warming than the net observed amount; cooling from aerosols offset part of that warming. Natural drivers and internal variability cannot explain the industrial-era global trend.
invalid_inferences: A high raw time-series correlation alone proves attribution.
Every warm or cool year must track annual emissions.
CO2 is the only climate driver.
All greenhouse gases can be physically collapsed into annual CO2-equivalent emissions without specifying the metric and time horizon.
